assumptions: That the alert's start and end timestamps are accurate and the condition genuinely lasted under one second, rather than the end timestamp being written by the same failure that prevented metrics from being read.
That the absence of retrieved metrics reflects a gap in the telemetry pipeline rather than a total outage of the service being measured; nothing in the record distinguishes these.
That io-shop sits on a customer-facing commerce path, inferred solely from its name.
That no customer impact occurred, inferred from the absence of reports and follow-on alerts rather than from any positive signal of healthy traffic.
That no remediation was needed, which follows from no cause having been found, not from any confirmation that the system is well.
input.executive_summary: An automated monitor reported an elevated error rate on one of our shop services and cleared itself immediately — the alert opened and closed within the same second. No customer reports, no follow-on alerts, and no supporting data were associated with it. The automated investigator attempted to pull metrics for the affected period, found none, and escalated without a finding. No remediation was performed and nothing was changed, because there was nothing identifiable to change. Any customer impact, if it occurred at all, would have lasted a fraction of a second. The open question is not what broke but why the monitoring produced an alert it could not then substantiate; that belongs to the monitoring stack rather than to the shop service.
input.impact_weight_reason: This is a placeholder, not a measurement. The only input available is the service name, "io-shop", which suggests something on the shopping path but does not say whether it serves checkout, browsing, or an internal function; no request data, route breakdown, or traffic figures were retrieved. A mid-range weight is used to avoid asserting either that the path was pure revenue or that it carried none. If the service's role is confirmed, this number should be replaced rather than adjusted — and given that no error rate and no duration of consequence were established, the weight has little to act on regardless.
input.root_cause: Not determined. An error-rate alert fired on io-shop and closed itself in well under a second; the automated investigation retrieved no metrics for the incident window and read no logs, so there is no evidence on which to name a cause. It is not known whether real errors were served or whether the alert fired on a sampling artifact at the edge of the evaluation window.
